experiment: S7 mechanistic decomposition and local robustness

comparison_information.all_policies_observe: current demand state, exact current competence state, the same physical transition laws, reward and complete feasible actions
comparison_information.demand_law: same initial distribution and Markov transition matrix in each paired policy comparison; Bellman uses the known matrix in continuation, reactive policy is defined to maximize only current CES and does not use future transition probabilities
comparison_information.transfer_access: Bellman and reactive variants with transfer have the same optional-teaching action catalog; without-transfer variants share the same MIS-only catalog
comparison_information.objective: cumulative existing CES; functional completion and resource metrics are diagnostics, not alternate objectives
comparison_information.future_realization: not revealed to the action selector; only current demand is observed
comparison_information.information_fairness: same state and model information is available to both policy classes; their use of future-demand probabilities differs by the intended planning mechanism. Both exact references know the true competence state, so these are oracle comparisons, not deployable hidden-competence policies.

sensitivity_protocol.method: center plus symmetric one-factor-at-a-time perturbations; all other settings held fixed
sensitivity_protocol.justification: Moderate symmetric local changes, interior to valid domains; eta perturbation is restricted to the bottleneck learner-skill cell; efficacy is restricted to the teaching relation used by the candidate action. No parameter chosen by maximizing policy differences.
